sentences: A monotone graph property is preserved when edges are added, and a graph property ignores vertex labels.
The randomized evasiveness conjecture asks whether every nontrivial such property on k vertices requires \(\Omega\)(k squared) adjacency queries for exact recognition with bounded error.
The algorithm must distinguish every yes-instance from every no-instance, including graphs differing by very few edges.
This differs fundamentally from property testing, which allows a gap between valid graphs and graphs far from validity.
A quadratic lower bound would say that randomness cannot avoid inspecting a constant fraction of potential edges in the worst case.
